name: King of Lasharon
overview: The King of Lasharon was a male ruler known primarily for being one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. His tribal affiliation and further personal details are not recorded in Scripture. This king's significance is tied to his role as an opponent subdued under God's guidance through Joshua.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Lasharon' directly identifies him as the ruler of the city or region of Lasharon. The name means simply 'king of Lasharon' and is not given by God but serves as a descriptive title found in Joshua 12:18.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Lasharon beyond his status as a defeated king listed among others in Joshua 12:18.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Lasharon represents the opposition to God's people during their divinely appointed conquest of the Promised Land. His defeat by Joshua illustrates God's faithfulness in granting victory over established Canaanite rulers. This event underscores the fulfillment of God's promise to Israel and the establishment of His people in the land.
